In natural language , a determiner , also called a determinative ( abbreviated det ), is a word or affix that is used with/precedes a noun to express its reference . [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Examples in English include articles ( the and a/an ), demonstratives ( this , that ), possessive determiners ( my, their ), and quantifiers ( many , both ). Not all languages have determiners, and not all systems of grammatical description recognize them as a distinct category.
